developerTrial.method: Scripted: README commands executed literally from a clean clone, packed tarball, temporary HOME and npm cache, and PATH-only invocation.

friction.symptom: v0.3–v0.6 regressions need benchmarks/checkouts/*, which is gitignored and was never recreated by any script; a clean checkout silently reports 0 tasks as N/A / recall 0
friction.rootCause: pinned repositories were cloned by hand during development (hidden state)
friction.fix: benchmarks/fetch-checkouts.ts (npm run benchmark:checkouts) fetches each pinned commit (sparse for keycloak); benchmark:v03 runs it first

friction.step: [v0.9] README tarball validation in a fresh clone
friction.symptom: `npm pack` fails in a fresh clone because prepack runs tsc before dependencies are installed; README also named context-slice-0.8.0.tgz and said 'Only Java source is supported in v0.7' / 'After linking ContextSlice'
friction.rootCause: README written from an already-installed development checkout
friction.fix: README adds `npm ci` before `npm pack`, names the current tarball, and drops stale version wording
friction.regressionTest: tests/package-metadata.test.ts (README tarball name matches package version)

friction.step: [v0.9] git status in target repository after init
friction.symptom: `?? .context-slice/` appears in the developer's git status
friction.rootCause: cache directory was not ignored and ContextSlice (correctly) does not edit the repository .gitignore
friction.fix: cache directory writes its own `.gitignore` containing `*`; also applied to caches created by 0.8.0 on first use after upgrade

friction.symptom: v0.8 report printed 'Path with spaces: false' and 'Nested cwd: false' while claiming status pass
friction.rootCause: macOS tmpdir is a symlink (/var -> /private/var); the check compared the symlinked path with the real path the CLI reports
friction.fix: smoke test uses realpathSync for its workspace

friction.symptom: no documented way to remove repository caches; uninstall leaves them
friction.rootCause: undocumented behavior
friction.fix: README documents `rm -rf .context-slice`; no `clean` command added (one rm is simpler than a new CLI surface)
friction.regressionTest: clean-room RC run (uninstall step verifies cache retention)

friction.symptom: `status` on a never-initialized repository creates an empty .context-slice/ cache while reporting UNINITIALIZED
friction.rootCause: IndexStorage opens (and creates) the SQLite cache on every command
friction.fix: accepted: the directory is self-ignored and contains no source; documented that ContextSlice only writes to .context-slice/

friction.symptom: a non-SQLite index.sqlite produced `INTERNAL_ERROR: file is not a database` (exit 1) and advised `context-slice doctor`, which fails the same way
friction.rootCause: SQLite open errors were not mapped to the existing INDEX_CORRUPT workflow error
friction.fix: IndexStorage raises INDEX_CORRUPT (exit 2) with remediation `rm -rf .context-slice && context-slice init`
friction.regressionTest: tests/cache.test.ts (corrupt cache fails with an actionable INDEX_CORRUPT error)

friction.step: [v0.9] Codex integration (codex exec with command context-slice, args [mcp])
friction.symptom: codex-cli 0.153.4 ended the turn with 'You've hit your usage limit' before any MCP tool call
friction.rootCause: assistant account quota on this host, not ContextSlice
friction.fix: none needed in ContextSlice; the RC script now reports a pre-tool runtime failure as DEFERRED instead of FAIL. Rerun `npm run release:rc -- --assistants` once quota resets

friction.step: [v0.9] preview on spring-petclinic: "explain the owner update flow"
friction.symptom: target resolves to OwnerController.initUpdateOwnerForm (the GET form handler) with 1 item / 32 tokens, and no callers or callees; processUpdateOwnerForm is the more useful target
friction.rootCause: task-text target ranking prefers the first matching handler; ranking changes are feature work outside v0.9 scope
friction.fix: accepted for v0.9; name the symbol in the task (e.g. "explain processUpdateOwnerForm") for a richer slice

friction.symptom: package version moved 0.9.0 -> 1.0.0; README, CHANGELOG, release notes and tests reference the new tarball name
friction.rootCause: planned release step, not a defect
friction.fix: package.json is the single source of truth; tests/package-metadata.test.ts asserts the version and that README names context-slice-<version>.tgz

friction.symptom: codex exec connected and called context.preview, but Codex refused it: 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never'
friction.rootCause: validation harness ran codex exec without an approval mode; non-interactive runs need --approve-for-me. Not a ContextSlice defect: the server connected, the tool was visible and the arguments were correct
friction.fix: clean-room script passes --approve-for-me; rerun succeeded and returned the expected target symbol

friction.symptom: upgrade and downgrade steps reported FAIL although the recorded behavior was correct
friction.rootCause: the assertions hard-coded the previous version as 0.8.0 while the v1.0 baseline is 0.9.0
friction.fix: assertions read the baseline version from the baseline checkout's package.json

friction.symptom: every source file of 32KB or more was silently skipped, including Excalidraw's 454KB App.tsx
friction.rootCause: the tree-sitter node binding rejects a string input of 32KB or more; the parse threw and was recorded only as a parse error
friction.fix: parse through a chunked input callback (4KB slices)
friction.regressionTest: benchmark parse-error counts (nest-core 0, excalidraw 4 of 597) plus tests/typescript.test.ts parse-error case

friction.symptom: UNIQUE constraint failure on symbols.id when two declarations shared a canonical identity
friction.rootCause: the TypeScript parser did not disambiguate duplicate identities the way the Java parser does
friction.fix: append #n to duplicate identities and repoint their call edges

friction.symptom: top-level statements produced no call edges, so a small app showed almost no calls
friction.rootCause: calls were only attributed to enclosing callables, and much TypeScript code lives at module scope
friction.fix: a synthetic module symbol named after the file owns top-level statements and their calls

friction.step: v1.1 build after fetching TypeScript benchmark checkouts
friction.symptom: npm run build compiled the checked-out third-party TypeScript repositories and failed
friction.rootCause: tsconfig included benchmarks/**/*.ts and the new checkouts are TypeScript
friction.fix: tsconfig excludes benchmarks/checkouts and tests/fixtures
friction.regressionTest: npm test (package smoke runs npm pack, which builds)

friction.symptom: a synthetic module symbol named after the file's basename collided with an exported symbol of the same name, making preview targets ambiguous
friction.rootCause: module symbols were named after the basename
friction.fix: module symbols are named by file path, which cannot shadow a declared symbol

friction.symptom: missing required facts were attributed to missing type resolution when they were really neighbouring declarations the slice did not include
friction.rootCause: coarse attribution heuristic in the benchmark script
friction.fix: TYPE_RESOLUTION is claimed only when the fact sits behind a call the resolver could not follow; otherwise CONTEXT_COMPOSITION
friction.regressionTest: benchmark report records the attribution per fact

friction.symptom: two required facts about sibling class members are not in the slice for a method target
friction.rootCause: a preview for a method includes callers and callees, not the rest of the enclosing class
friction.fix: accepted and reported: required-fact recall is 95.56%, not 100%, and the gap is attributed to context composition rather than hidden

friction.symptom: the 1.0.0 CLI cannot use a cache written by 1.1.0: it exits 1 with a SQLite error until `.context-slice` is deleted
friction.rootCause: the 1.1.0 schema adds a NOT NULL language column, and the already-released 1.0.0 code inserts without it. 1.0.0 cannot be changed retroactively
friction.fix: documented in the changelog, release notes and docs/typescript-support.md: downgrading requires `rm -rf .context-slice`. No data is misread; the failure is loud. Forward upgrades and same-shape schema changes rebuild automatically
friction.regressionTest: clean-room downgrade step asserts the failure is loud and that cleanup restores it

friction.symptom: `init` reported "Indexed 10 Java files" in a TypeScript repository, and `doctor` labelled its check "java-source"
friction.rootCause: wording predating multi-language support
friction.fix: init reports source files with a per-language breakdown; the doctor check is named "source"
friction.regressionTest: tests/cli.test.ts and tests/typescript.test.ts assert the wording
